Basis: Law 90-11 of 21 April 1990 on labour relations, the articles on termination and dismissal (art. 66 grounds of termination; art. 73 dismissal for serious fault and its list; art. 73-1 the disciplinary procedure: written, reasoned notice and hearing of the worker; art. 73-2 notice period; art. 73-3 dismissal in breach of the procedure; art. 73-4 dismissal without real and serious cause) as amended by Law 91-29 and Ordinance 96-21.

Is the plaintiff a worker under a contract of employment governed by Law 90-11, and not a civil servant (Ordinance 06-03, administrative courts) or a member of a category excluded by art. 3 or 4 of Law 90-11 (military, magistrates, special statutes)?
Element: the employment relation exists and its start date (contract, pay slips, social-security affiliation; the contract may be proved by any means, art. 10 of Law 90-11).
Element: the dismissal by the employer and its date (dismissal letter, or a factual dismissal: refusal of access, stopping of pay).

Element: the fault relied on by the employer is not a serious fault within art. 73, or the employer cannot prove it; who bears the burden of proving the fault and the regularity of the procedure (the employer, by my memory of art. 73-4 and case law).
Element: the procedure of art. 73-1 (written notification of the decision, hearing of the worker, assistance by a worker of his choice) was not respected, and the internal regulation's procedure.

Distinguish the two sanctions: procedural irregularity (art. 73-3: annulment and order to follow the procedure, plus compensation not below the monthly salary?) versus abusive dismissal on the merits (art. 73-4: reinstatement with acquired advantages, or if either party refuses, compensation not less than six months' salary, without prejudice to other damages).
Request: reinstatement in the post with the advantages acquired; the employer or the worker may refuse reinstatement, which turns the remedy into compensation.
Request: compensation not less than six months of salary, plus further damages if any; the amount of the salary must be stated.

Accessory requests: unpaid wages, notice-period compensation, dismissal indemnity (art. 73-2 or collective agreement), work certificate, interest, costs, provisional execution of right for wages (Law 90-04).
Mandatory prior step: internal grievance procedure inside the employer (Law 90-04, art. 3 to 5) before going to the labour inspectorate.
Mandatory prior step: conciliation before the conciliation office at the labour inspectorate (Law 90-04, art. 19 and following); a record of non-conciliation must be attached to the petition.
Exceptions to prior conciliation: defendant domiciled abroad; employer under judicial settlement or bankruptcy (Law 90-04 art. 19 as amended); check whether the text still says so.
If a conciliation record (agreement) was drawn up, the claim is replaced by enforcement of the agreement (Law 90-04 art. 33 onward); the court is not seized of the same dispute.
Time limit: the petition must be filed within six months from delivery of the non-conciliation record, under pain of forfeiture of the right of action (CPCM art. 504; also Law 90-04 art. 36?).

How the six months are counted: CPCM art. 405 (full periods, dies a quo not counted, last day extended if holiday), months counted calendar to calendar; who raises the forfeiture (of public order? court of its own motion?).
Lifting of forfeiture by order of the court president for force majeure (CPCM art. 322).
Effect of an earlier non-conciliation record for the same dispute: does a second record restart the six months?
Competent section: the social section of the court (CPCM art. 500); composition with labour assessors (art. 502); if the court has no social section.

Territorial jurisdiction: the court of the place where the work is performed; or the court of the worker's domicile when the contract was suspended or broken by a work accident or occupational disease (CPCM art. 501); this rule is of public order?
Judgments in first and last instance for certain labour matters (Law 90-04 art. 21: annulment of disciplinary sanctions, certificates, pay slips), with provisional execution; and appeal otherwise.
Economic dismissal / reduction of staff (Legislative Decree 94-09, art. 69 to 71 of Law 90-11) is a different regime with its own procedure.
Resignation, retirement, end of a fixed-term contract, or the worker's abandonment of post are not dismissals; a fixed-term contract concluded outside art. 12 cases is deemed indefinite.
Dismissal of a staff delegate or union representative needs special protection (Law 90-14 art. 53 and following): nullity and reinstatement as of right.
A dismissal following a criminal prosecution of the worker: the effect of the criminal case on the civil one (the criminal holds the civil in abeyance, CPP art. 4).

If the employer is a public administrative body and the worker a civil servant, the claim leaves the ordinary courts (CPCM art. 800-801); if the employer is a public body under private law with contract workers, the social section stays competent.
Limitation of wage claims: periodic renewable rights, five years (Civil Code art. 309); some claims by workers for wages: one year (Civil Code art. 311?).
Formal notice is not required before a dismissal claim (no contractual default); check whether the formal-notice module applies to the damages request.
Documents: non-conciliation record, contract or proof of employment, dismissal decision, pay slips, internal regulation, certificate of social-security affiliation.
Petition formal elements (CPCM art. 15) and the fees: labour petitions by workers may be exempt from judicial fees (Law 90-04 / finance law).

Amendments to remember: Ordinance 96-21 rewrote art. 73-4 (reinstatement or compensation of at least six months); Law 91-29 rewrote art. 73 to 73-4; CPCM 08-09 (2008) and its 2022 amendment (Law 22-13) on the social section and the specialised courts.
